To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
all-trans- RA is teratogenic for mouse embryos in vitro.
all-trans- RA (tretinion) inhibits embryonic growth and is teratogenic to mouse embryos in whole embryo culture, causing hypoplasia and/or reduction deformities of craniofacial tissues.
retinoic acid is teratogenic for mouse embryos cultured in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of retinoic on craniofacial and limb development of mice in whole embryo culture.
the effects of retinoic acids and retinoids in the development of mouse embryos in culture.
the teratogenic effect of all-trans- RA in mouse embryos in culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all-trans- RA is teratogenic and causes craniofacial malformations in mouse embryos in culture.
all-trans- RA, in the concentrations used in the present study, was teratogenic in whole embryo culture.
retinoids, in particular retinoids of natural origin, are not teratogenic in mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the teratogenic effect of RA in whole embryo culture is due to a direct inhibition of cell proliferation.
all-trans- RA inhibits the development of the craniofacially developing mouse embryos in vitro.
all-trans- retinoic acid is a potent teratogen in mouse whole embryo cultures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RA is a teratogen in mouse whole embryo cultures and that the teratogenic effects are dose-dependent.
the retinoic acid receptor antagonist, BMS 189, has the potential to reduce the teratogenicity of retinoic acids in the mouse embryo.
retinoic acid can have a significant impact on craniofacial and limb development in mice.
